question: Which of Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, or Micron will post the highest percentage change in closing share price from the November 13, 2026 close to the November 27, 2026 close?

calls.reasoning: Prior: four highly correlated chip names over a 2-week window start near 25% each; higher-volatility names (AMD, MU) get a slight edge for the max, and Broadcom (lowest vol) is shaded down. NVDA has an idiosyncratic catalyst (Q3 FY27 earnings Nov 17, first under interim CEO Kress; options imply ~8.3% move), which raises its variance, and it sits at a depressed valuation after the Huang exit, so a relief rally is plausible. Good NVDA results would also lift MU (HBM supplier). An unconfirmed-date report of a premarket rebound (NVDA +4%, AMD/MU +6%) was not weighted heavily. Market check: no Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold/bookmaker contract matching this question found; a Lines.com contract on NVDA closing above $150 on Nov 13 is not comparable.

- Broadcom closed Nov 13 at $347.01, -4.76% (stockanalysis/247wallst search summary, Nov 13).
- AMD fell ~10-11% on Nov 13, trading near $523 intraday (247wallst, Nov 13); the exact close was not verified.
- MU fell ~4-5% Nov 13, intraday ~$767, Friday low $750.25, after-hours $761.20 (Yahoo/financefeeds, Nov 13-15). One preview says MU is 'up 12.8% into Nvidia week' (financefeeds).

- MU sells HBM to NVDA, so NVDA results feed through to memory names.
- A TradingKey premarket report (date not fully verified, possibly Nov 16) shows NVDA +4%, AMD and MU +6%, and CoreWeave +16% on its debt/guidance news.
- Volatility ordering: AMD and MU have the highest realized daily moves recently (5-11%), AVGO the lowest of the four, and NVDA elevated by the CEO shock.
- The 1-year return leader is MU (~+293%), ahead of AMD (~+98%) (NerdWallet, Nov 2).
- Status quo: no information on relative performance after Nov 13. Base rate for an equal-vol 4-way race is 25% each; high-vol names are favored somewhat for the max.

calls.reconciliation: The runs agree on structure (near-uniform, AVGO shaded down) and differ by at most 2 points. Factual: the MU Nov 13 close is reported as $773.07 or $778.31. I could not settle it without web access, and it does not affect the ranking. The premarket rebound report (NVDA +4%, AMD/MU +6%) has an unverified date and is not a close, so it gets almost no weight. The claimed AVGO weekly rally of 18-24% conflicts with the Nov 13 -4.76% close; I could not settle it and it matters little. Judgment: how much to favour high-vol AMD/MU versus NVDA's earnings variance. No evidence breaks the tie, so I set NVDA, AMD and MU equal and kept AVGO's lower-vol discount, which I carried forward from Run 1.
